content.value_statement: Competitor information is scattered across websites, reviews, and SEO reports. This skill organizes available evidence into dated profiles and comparable summaries.
actual_capabilities: Guide quick scans or deep profiles covering competitor positioning, features, pricing, customers, and content strategy.
Use Firecrawl or WebFetch to collect key website pages and optional review sources.
Incorporate traffic estimates, keyword rankings, backlinks, and organic competitors from connected SEO tools.
Save raw research in dated local folders and generate one Markdown profile per competitor.
Create comparison summaries with shared metrics, positioning maps, and strategic observations.
Update existing profiles with refreshed evidence and a change log while preserving earlier raw snapshots.
limitations: Live research requires working browsing tools; quantitative SEO metrics require a connected data provider.
Research calls can consume paid API credits; deep profiles require more requests than quick scans.
Blocked pages and JavaScript-rendered content can leave fields unavailable or unconfirmed.
Profiles are dated snapshots; observed website claims and traffic estimates do not independently prove customer counts or feature absence.

use_cases.title: Compare Market Positioning
use_cases.description: Compare competitor messaging, pricing, and audience signals against your product using consistent profiles and evidence labels.

use_cases.title: Identify Organic Search Opportunities
use_cases.description: Review competitor keywords, top pages, backlinks, and content themes to identify research-backed content opportunities.

use_cases.title: Monitor Competitive Changes
use_cases.description: Refresh dated competitor profiles and document observed pricing or product changes before product planning discussions.

prompt_templates.title: Start With a Quick Scan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a quick profile for [competitor URL]. Summarize positioning and public pricing, and cite the pages checked with the research date.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Competitor Pricing
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [competitor URLs] against [our product]. Focus on pricing and positioning. Create individual profiles and a comparison summary. Mark missing data explicitly.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Compare a focused competitor list.

prompt_templates.title: Research a Competitor in Depth
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a deep profile for [competitor URL] using available scraping and SEO tools. Include reviews, keywords, backlinks, and source dates. Separate observations from inferences.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Combine website evidence with connected market data.

prompt_templates.title: Refresh a Competitive Landscape
prompt_templates.prompt: Update existing profiles for [competitor URLs]. Preserve prior raw snapshots and create dated research folders. Add sourced change logs and refresh the summary. Flag unverified advantages.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: Maintain evidence across repeated research runs.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: Quickly profile a competitor from its homepage and pricing page without SEO tools.
output: Profile: Sample Workspace. Depth: Quick scan. Sources: Supplied homepage and pricing captures dated 2026-10-20.
Observed: The homepage emphasizes shared team workflows. The pricing capture lists a free plan and a paid team plan.
Unavailable: Organic traffic and keyword metrics, because no SEO provider is connected.
Inferred: Team collaboration appears central to positioning. Feature gaps require documentation or trial verification.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: Compare two competitors using their supplied pricing captures and positioning notes.
output: Comparison: Sample Alpha emphasizes self-service setup; Sample Beta emphasizes enterprise support.
Pricing: Alpha publishes plan prices. Beta requests sales contact. Enterprise pricing remains unconfirmed.
Implication: Test whether transparent pricing matters to our target buyers before changing our positioning.
Deliverables: Two competitor profiles, one landscape summary, and dated raw source folders.

best_practices: Provide competitor URLs, your product context, research depth, and priority dimensions before starting.
Use consistent metrics and source dates across competitors, and preserve raw evidence in dated folders.
Separate observations, inferences, and implications; verify suspected feature gaps before using them in public claims.
anti_patterns: Treating missing website information as proof that a competitor lacks a feature.
Presenting SEO estimates, customer logos, or unsupported advantages as independently verified facts.
Requesting deep research across a large competitor list without priorities or API cost awareness.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide competitor URLs, your product context, preferred depth, and focus areas. Existing product-marketing context can supply background information.

faq.question: Which tools does the workflow use?
faq.answer: The preferred stack is Firecrawl and DataForSEO. Alternatives include WebFetch and connected SEO providers such as Ahrefs, Semrush, or Ubersuggest.

faq.question: Can I research competitors without an SEO provider?
faq.answer: Yes, if browsing tools are available. The workflow marks unavailable metrics and proceeds with qualitative website observations.

faq.question: What is the difference between a quick scan and a deep profile?
faq.answer: A quick scan focuses on homepage, pricing, and summary SEO data. A deep profile adds broader pages, reviews, and detailed competitive metrics.

faq.question: Where are profiles and research sources saved?
faq.answer: Profiles and the comparison summary are saved under competitor-profiles/. Raw scrapes, SEO responses, and reviews use competitor-specific dated subfolders.

faq.question: Does this skill create comparison pages or sales battle cards?
faq.answer: No. It produces research profiles and summaries. The documentation points to separate skills for comparison pages and sales battle cards.
